subproblem.title: Potential estimate over a set of finite measure: ∫_S |w|^{1−n} ≤ (n+1)·ω^{1−1/n}·Lⁿ(S)^{1/n} (radius split of Step 5)
subproblem.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1, and let ω := Lⁿ(B_1(0)) ∈ (0,∞), as a real number. Let S ⊆ ℝⁿ = Eucl n be a Borel-measurable set (MeasurableSet S) with Lⁿ(S) < ∞, and write L := Lⁿ(S) ∈ [0,∞), as a real number. Then w ↦ (|w|^m)⁻¹ is integrable on S, and ∫_S (|w|^m)⁻¹ dw ≤ (m + 2)·ω^{m/(m+1)}·L^{1/(m+1)} (real powers).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (S : Set (Eucl (m + 1))), MeasurableSet S → volume S ≠ ⊤ → IntegrableOn (fun t : Eucl (m + 1) => (‖t‖ ^ m)⁻¹) S ∧ ∫ t in S, (‖t‖ ^ m)⁻¹ ≤ ((m : ℝ) + 2) * (volume (ball (0 : Eucl (m + 1)) 1)).toReal ^ ((m : ℝ) / ((m : ℝ) + 1)) * (volume S).toReal ^ ((1 : ℝ) / ((m : ℝ) + 1))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the radius split in Step 5 of the parent proof. This is the elementary form of the potential estimate of Gilbarg–Trudinger §7.8 (proof of Lemma 7.12), with the cruder constant n + 1 in place of n. Write f(w) := (|w|^m)⁻¹ = |w|^{1−n}.

1. Preliminaries. f ≥ 0, and f is Borel measurable (norm, power, inverse). ω > 0 because B_1(0) is a nonempty open set (measure_ball_pos), and ω < ∞ (measure_ball_lt_top).

2. Bound away from the origin. Let ρ > 0 and w ∈ S ∖ B_ρ(0). Then |w| ≥ ρ > 0, so |w|^m ≥ ρ^m > 0 and f(w) ≤ (ρ^m)⁻¹ (pow_le_pow_left₀, inv_anti₀). Also Lⁿ(S ∖ B_ρ(0)) ≤ Lⁿ(S) < ∞. Since f is measurable and bounded by (ρ^m)⁻¹ on S ∖ B_ρ(0), it is integrable there (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded).

3. Integrability on S. Fix ρ > 0. By radial_ball_integral, f is integrable on B_ρ(0), hence on S ∩ B_ρ(0) ⊆ B_ρ(0). With Step 2, f is integrable on (S ∩ B_ρ(0)) ∪ (S ∖ B_ρ(0)) = S. Taking ρ = 1 proves the first claim.

4. Case L = 0. Lⁿ(S) is finite and L = 0, so Lⁿ(S) = 0. Then the restriction of Lⁿ to S is the zero measure, and ∫_S f = 0. The right-hand side is (m + 2)·ω^{m/(m+1)}·0^{1/(m+1)} = 0, because 1/(m+1) ≠ 0 (Real.zero_rpow). So the inequality reads 0 ≤ 0.

5. Case L > 0: the radius. Let p := 1/(m+1) and ρ := (L/ω)^p > 0. Then ρ^{m+1} = (L/ω)^{p·(m+1)} = L/ω (Real.rpow_natCast, Real.rpow_mul). That is, L = ω·ρ^{m+1}.

6. Split. B_ρ(0) is measurable and f is integrable on S (Step 3). So ∫_S f = ∫_{S∩B_ρ(0)} f + ∫_{S∖B_ρ(0)} f (integral_inter_add_sdiff).

7. Near part. f ≥ 0 is integrable on B_ρ(0), and S ∩ B_ρ(0) ⊆ B_ρ(0). So setIntegral_mono_set and radial_ball_integral give ∫_{S∩B_ρ(0)} f ≤ ∫_{B_ρ(0)} f = (m + 1)·ω·ρ.

8. Far part. f and the constant (ρ^m)⁻¹ are both integrable on the measurable set S∖B_ρ(0), which has finite measure. By Step 2 and setIntegral_mono_on, ∫_{S∖B_ρ(0)} f ≤ ∫_{S∖B_ρ(0)} (ρ^m)⁻¹ = Lⁿ(S∖B_ρ(0))·(ρ^m)⁻¹ ≤ L·(ρ^m)⁻¹ = ω·ρ^{m+1}/ρ^m = ω·ρ.

9. Hence ∫_S f ≤ (m + 1)·ω·ρ + ω·ρ = (m + 2)·ω·ρ.

10. Rewriting. (L/ω)^p = L^p/ω^p (Real.div_rpow; L, ω ≥ 0). Also ω/ω^p = ω^{1−p} (Real.rpow_sub, ω > 0), and 1 − p = m/(m+1). So (m + 2)·ω·ρ = (m + 2)·ω^{m/(m+1)}·L^{1/(m+1)}, which is the claimed bound. ∎
proof_key_steps: f = |w|^{1−n} ≤ ρ^{−m} off B_ρ(0), so f is integrable on S∖B_ρ(0). With radial_ball_integral, f is integrable on S.
If Lⁿ(S) = 0, both sides vanish. Otherwise take ρ = (L/ω)^{1/(m+1)}, so that L = ω·ρ^{m+1}.

audit.reason: Borel measurability, finite measure, integrability, and the real-power bound match exactly. The proof establishes integrability before splitting the integral, handles zero measure, and justifies the optimized radius and power identities for positive measure. Its only sibling dependency is radial_ball_integral.
